questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay titled “Doviolent video games lead to violence?”. The statement given below is for your reference. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words . A growing body of research finds that violent video games can make kids act aggressively in their real world relationships, causing an increase in violence.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Do violent video games lead to violence? While a growing body of research suggests such games can make players more aggressive, I believe they do not directly cause real violence; rather, their influence depends on the individual and the surrounding environment.

To begin with, exposure to violent scenes may indeed shape behavior. First, children who spend hours shooting and fighting on screen can gradually treat aggression as normal, and some may copy what they see when they lose their temper. However, most players clearly separate games from reality. A well-supervised teenager, for instance, can enjoy an action game after homework and still behave kindly toward classmates, because family guidance and self-control matter far more than the game itself.

In conclusion, violent video games alone do not turn ordinary people into violent ones. What truly counts is proper parental supervision and healthy habits. Therefore, rather than simply blaming the games, parents and schools should teach children to play in moderation and to tell fantasy from real life.

transcript.text: And finally in tonight's news, a 9-year-old boy named Joe, told not to draw in class, wins a job decorating a restaurant with his drawings. Rather than shutting down the habit of drawing in his school's workbook, Joe's parents decided to encourage his creativity by sending their son to an after-school art class. His teacher recognized Joe's talent and posted all his work online, which led to something pretty wonderful.

questions.stem: What did Joe's parents decide to do?

options.text: Enrol him in a Newcastle football club.
Send him to an after-school art class.
Forbid him to draw in his workbook.
Help him post his drawings online.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Rather than shutting down the habit of drawing in his school's workbook, Joe's parents decided to encourage his creativity by sending their son to an after-school art class.信号：Rather than后的转折落点 。答案信号是句首的 Rather than shutting down the habit of drawing——"而不是去扼杀"。Rather than 是一个含蓄否定的转折标…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 说"给他报名 Newcastle 足球俱乐部"。录音确实念到了 He's great at football. 和地名 Newcastle，但那是第3段描述乔"球踢得好"，第2段 Newcastle 是餐厅所在地，根本没有"父母给他报足球队"这回事。它把零散原词拼成了假事件。 借用原文：shutting down the habit of drawing in his school's workbook
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：C 说"禁止他在练习册上画画"。录音里 shutting down the habit of drawing in his school's workbook 确实提到"扼杀在练习册上画画的习惯"，但它前面有 Rather than——是父母"没有"做的事。C 恰恰取了被转折否定掉的那半句，方向反了。 借用原文：His teacher recognized Joe's talent and posted all his work online
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：D 说"帮他把画发到网上"。录音里 His teacher recognized Joe's talent and posted all his work online 确实有"发到网上"，但做这件事的是"老师"，不是"父母"。题问的是父母，把老师的行为安到父母头上，张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（sending their son to an after-school art class ↔ Send him to an after-school art class. 几乎原句对应）

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音确实说她 posted an image of a man suspected of stealing the dog，B 盗用了这里的 suspect 原词，但发嫌疑人照片是她找狗路上的一个中间手段，不是她『努力要达成』的目的，答非所问。 借用原文：Police are investigating the incident.

optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音说她 posted a tearful video on social media，D 盗用 social media、post 原词，但发社交媒体只是她为找回狗采取的途径，跟 B 一样是手段而非她要达成的目的。

transcript.text: London's Eggs & Bread café offers boiled eggs, toast, jam, and bacon, as well as tea, coffee and orange juice. But at the end of the meal, customers don't have to worry about the bill. Hungry customers can pay whatever amount they can afford to eat at the café, or nothing at all.
transcript.zh: 伦敦的Eggs & Bread咖啡馆提供煮鸡蛋、吐司、果酱和培根,以及茶、咖啡和橙汁。但在用餐结束时,顾客不必担心账单。饥饿的顾客可以支付他们能承受的任何金额在这家咖啡馆用餐,或者什么都不付。

transcript.text: Owner Guy Wilson says his café aims to build community, rather than profits. He wants to provide a bridge for people to connect in an area that has been divided by class and wealth by providing affordable breakfasts.
transcript.zh: 店主Guy Wilson说,他的咖啡馆旨在建立社区,而非追求利润。他希望通过提供人们负担得起的早餐,为这个被阶级和财富分割的地区的人们搭建一座连接的桥梁。

transcript.text: The café is open in the mornings every day of the year and has two members of staff or supervisors on shift every day. The café doesn't use volunteers, but pays its staff to ensure consistency in its service. It doesn't take donations and doesn't want to be seen as a charity.
transcript.zh: 这家咖啡馆全年每天早上营业,每天有两名员工或主管值班。咖啡馆不使用志愿者,而是支付员工工资以确保服务的一致性。它不接受捐赠,也不希望被视为慈善机构。

transcript.text: Mr. Wilson says, when people start to know other people around them, they realize they're not that different. And whatever their financial background, or their educational background, most people will have something in common with each other. He says it's important that his café can offer his customers security and permanence.
transcript.zh: Wilson先生说,当人们开始了解周围的其他人时,他们会意识到彼此并没有那么不同。无论他们的经济背景或教育背景如何,大多数人都会与彼此有一些共同点。他说,他的咖啡馆能够为顾客提供安全感和稳定性是很重要的。

questions.stem: What does Guy Wilson say his café aims to do?

options.text: Provide free meals to the local poor.
Help people connect with each other.
Help eliminate class difference in his area.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Owner Guy Wilson says his café aims to build community, rather than profits. He wants to provide a bridge for people to connect in an area that has been divided by class and wealth by providing affordable breakfasts.信号：表目的的 aims to / wants to 。这句里 aims to build community和 wants to provide a bridge for people to connect接连出现两个表…

optionAnalysis.A: 偷换概念：原文说店主靠 providing affordable breakfasts（提供负担得起的早餐）来搭桥，affordable 是"付得起、便宜"，并不等于 free（免费）；A 把"affordable"夸大成 free meals，又添了"the local poor（当地穷人）"这个原文没指明的对象，是听到"早餐"就误选的陷阱。 借用原文：has been divided by class and wealth
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：原文只说该地区 has been divided by class and wealth（被阶层和财富所割裂），店是想在这种环境里"搭桥连接"，从没说要 eliminate（消除）阶层差异。C 盗用了 class 这个原词，再把"搭桥"夸大成"消除差异"——听到 class 就选它正中陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：原文明确老板要的是 build community, rather than profits（营造社区而非利润），目标根本不在"服务档次"上；D 的 first-class service（一流服务）属于无中生有，还隐隐与"不追求利润"的取向相反，是用一个听起来"高大上"的褒义短语来诱选。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（provide a bridge for people to connect ↔ Help people connect with each other. 搭桥让人连接=帮人互相连接）

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The café doesn't use volunteers, but pays its staff to ensure consistency in its service.信号：否定 doesn't + 转折 but 。答案句靠 doesn't use volunteers这个明确否定，加上 but pays its staff的转折点出真意——"不用义工、改用付薪员工"。否定词与转折词同现…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：原文说店 doesn't take donations and doesn't want to be seen as a charity（不接受捐款、也不想被当成慈善机构）；B 盗用 donations / charity 两个原词，却说成 donates regularly to a local charity（定期向当地慈善机构捐款），方向完全反了——这是"听到 charity 就选"的高诱惑陷阱。 借用原文：is open in the mornings every day of the year

And whatever their financial background, or their educational background, most people will have something in common with each other.信号：条件 when + 结果 they realize / will have 。答案句以 when people start to know other people around them起头，后面 they rea…

transcript.text: 1 Pigs are not native to North America.
They were first introduced to California by Spanish and Russian explorers and settlers many centuries ago.
In the early times, pigs were allowed to wander freely in search of food.

This practice also allowed many pigs to escape from farms and live in the wild, which became a problem. 2 In fact, as one of the most damaging invasive species on the continent, wild pigs cause millions of dollars in crop damage yearly.
They also harbor dozens of diseases that threaten both humans and farm animals.
Forest patches with wild pigs have been found to have considerably reduced plant and animal diversity.
In addition to either eating other animals or their food supply, wild pigs damage native habitats by rooting up grasses and rubbing on trees.
Their activities may also create opportunities for invasive plants to colonize these areas.
Wild pigs will eat almost anything containing calories.
Mice, deer, birds, snakes and frogs are among their victims.
They can also harm other wild species through indirect competition, rather than eating them or shrinking their food supply.
On one particular United States island, wild pigs themselves became an attractive food source for a species of mainland eagle.
The eagles began breeding on the island, and also feeding on a species of native fox.
The foxes were almost wiped out completely.

transcript.text: The craft will use the heat of re-entry to roast coffee beans as they float inside it in a pressurised tank. The effect would be to roast the beans all over, and produce perfect coffee. The businessmen say that on Earth, beans can easily break apart and get burned in the roaster. But if gravity is removed, the beans float around in a heated oven, receiving 360 degrees of evenly distributed heat and roast to near perfection.
transcript.zh: 该航天器将利用再入大气层时产生的热量来烘焙咖啡豆,豆子会在一个加压舱内漂浮。这种方式能够全方位烘焙咖啡豆,制作出完美的咖啡。这两位商人表示,在地球上,咖啡豆在烘焙机中很容易破碎和烧焦。但如果去除重力,咖啡豆就会在加热的烤箱中四处漂浮,接受360度均匀分布的热量,烘焙至近乎完美的状态。

transcript.text: The spacecraft will reach a height of around 200 km. The beans would then be roasted in the heat generated by the craft's 20-minute re-entry into Earth's atmosphere. Temperatures in the pressurised tank will be kept to around 200℃.
transcript.zh: 航天器将到达约200公里的高度。随后咖啡豆将在航天器重返地球大气层的20分钟过程中,利用产生的热量进行烘焙。加压舱内的温度将保持在200℃左右。

transcript.text: Once back on Earth, the planet's first space-roasted beans would be used to make coffee that would be sold for the first time in Dubai. This is where the pair's company is based. It is not clear how much they would charge for a cup.
transcript.zh: 返回地球后,这些地球上首批太空烘焙的咖啡豆将被用来制作咖啡,并首次在Dubai销售。这正是这对创业者公司的所在地。目前尚不清楚他们会对一杯咖啡收取多少费用。

transcript.text: Surprisingly, the Space Roaster concept—should it go ahead—will not be the first attempt to take coffee into space. In 2015, two Italian companies collaborated on the construction of a similar type of spacecraft, which was the first coffee machine designed for use in space.
transcript.zh: 令人惊讶的是, Space Roaster概念——如果能够实施的话——将不是首次尝试将咖啡带入太空。2015年,两家意大利公司合作建造了一种类似的航天器,那是首台为太空使用而设计的咖啡机。

options.text: Taste coffee while in outer space.
Roast coffee beans in outer space.
Develop a new strain of coffee bean.
Use a pressurised tank to brew coffee.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A pair of entrepreneurs are planning to build and launch a spacecraft that would carry and roast coffee beans in outer space.信号：原文 planning to 与题干同词，是直接应答信号 。录音第一句就用 are planning to 直接对上题干的 planning to do，这种题干问什么、原文紧接着用同一表计划的词说出来的句子，就是答…

optionAnalysis.A: 答非所问：Taste coffee while in outer space. 借了后文做咖啡、卖咖啡的话题诱你联想到品尝，但原文这两人计划的是 roast 烘焙，从没说要在太空 taste 品尝咖啡，属答非所问。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：Develop a new strain of coffee bean. 说培育咖啡豆新品种，原文通篇只讲烘焙现有的豆子、从未提培育新品种，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：Use a pressurised tank to brew coffee. 盗用了原文 in a pressurised tank 这个真出现过的原词来骗你，但原文那个加压罐是用来 roast 烘焙豆子的，不是 brew 冲泡咖啡，听到熟词就选正中圈套。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（roast coffee beans in outer space ↔ Roast coffee beans in outer space. 原文短语与选项几乎逐词对应）

optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：They abandoned the attempt to roast coffee beans in space. 盗用原文 the first attempt to take coffee into space 里的 attempt，可原文是说2015年并非首次尝试、那两家公司是合作建成了机器，根本没说放弃，方向相反。

transcript.text: In cold and snowy Alaska, there's a village called Takotna. It has a population of a mere 49 souls. Each March, this tiny village swells up in numbers, because it is located in the middle of a race that takes place every year. It is a seven-day race, called the Iditarod Trail, and participants stop at Takotna for their obligatory 24-hour rest. Lucky for them, Takotna is famous for its delicious fruit pies.
transcript.zh: 在寒冷多雪的阿拉斯加，有一个名叫Takotna的村庄。它的人口仅有49人。每年三月，这个小村庄的人数会激增，因为它位于一年一度举行的比赛路线中途。这是一场为期七天的比赛，名为Iditarod Trail，参赛者会在Takotna停留进行规定的24小时休息。对他们来说幸运的是，Takotna以其美味的水果派而闻名。

transcript.text: Weeks before the competitors arrive, the residents of Takotna start preparing for what is without question their biggest event of the year. The whole village chips in to help, including the kids, who end up developing their baking skills at an early age. The exhausted and hungry racers are greeted with delightful pies of all kinds, such as apple, orange, lemon or banana. They consume the pies as stomach warming race fuel. The toughness of the race allows for racers to eat pretty much whatever they want. The more calories, the better.
transcript.zh: 在参赛者到来前几周，Takotna的居民就开始为这场毫无疑问是他们全年最盛大的活动做准备。全村人都参与帮忙，包括孩子们，他们因此在很小的时候就开始培养烘焙技能。筋疲力尽且饥肠辘辘的参赛者会受到各种美味派的款待，比如苹果派、橙子派、柠檬派或香蕉派。他们将这些派作为暖胃的比赛燃料来食用。比赛的艰苦程度使得参赛者几乎可以想吃什么就吃什么。卡路里越高越好。

transcript.text: Takotna has gained a reputation for its dessert-based hospitality since the 1970s. It started with one person, Jan Newton. Jan moved from Idaho with her husband in 1972 and opened a restaurant. Her rich and filling-fruit pies quickly got the racers' attention, and the village gained some fame as a result. Proud residents then started to refer to Jan as Queen of Takotna.
transcript.zh: 自20世纪70年代以来，Takotna因其以甜点为特色的热情好客而声名远扬。这一切始于一个人，Jan Newton。Jan和她的丈夫在1972年从Idaho搬来，并开了一家餐厅。她制作的香浓饱腹的水果派很快引起了参赛者的注意，村庄也因此获得了一些名气。自豪的居民随后开始称Jan为Takotna女王。

questions.stem: Why do a lot of people come to the village of Takotna every March?

options.text: It is the best time for sightseeing.
A race passes through it annually.
They come to clean the Iditarod Trail.
It is when the villagers choose a queen.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Each March, this tiny village swells up in numbers, because it is located in the middle of a race that takes place every year.信号：因果连词 because 引出真因 。这句的答案信号是因果连词 because：题干问 "为什么三月人多"，录音正好用 because it is located in the middle of a race th…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：It is the best time for sightseeing. 说三月是观光最佳时节，但录音只讲了比赛带来人流，全程没提观光或景色好坏，属凭常识脑补出来的理由。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：They come to clean the Iditarod Trail. 偷用了录音里真出现过的赛事名 Iditarod Trail 来骗 "听到就想选"，但录音说人们是来参赛/被吸引，根本没说来 "打扫"（clean）这条小径，盗了名字却安了个录音没有的动作。 借用原文：Proud residents then started to refer to Jan as Queen of Takotna
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：It is when the villagers choose a queen. 借了录音末尾 started to refer to Jan as Queen of Takotna（村民称 Jan 为 "塔科特纳王后"）里的 queen 一词，但那只是对一个人的尊称，并非 "三月选王后" 的活动，更不是人们来访的原因，把后文的称呼挪来当来访理由。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a race that takes place every year ↔ A race passes through it annually takes place every year = annually）

questions.stem: What is the village of Takotna famous for?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Lucky for them, Takotna is famous for its delicious fruit pies.信号：标志短语 famous for 直接点题 。答案信号就是题干同款短语 famous for：录音原话 Takotna is famous for its delicious fruit pies 与题干 famous…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Its children's baking skills. 搬用了录音里真出现的 developing their baking skills（孩子们练就烘焙手艺），但录音说孩子练手艺只是全村备战的一个细节，村子 "出名" 的点录音明确说是水果派，不是孩子的手艺——盗了 baking skills 却答非所问。 借用原文：In cold and snowy Alaska
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：Its unique winter scenery. 说村子以独特冬景闻名，录音开头确实提到 cold and snowy Alaska（寒冷多雪的阿拉斯加）这一背景，但从没说村子靠 "冬景" 出名，是把 "地处雪国" 脑补成了 "以雪景著称"。 借用原文：delightful pies of all kinds, such as apple, orange, lemon or banana
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：Its great food variety. 借了第二段 pies of all kinds, such as apple, orange, lemon or banana（各种口味的派）的 "多样" 印象，但那是在讲招待racers的派有多种口味，而村子 "出名" 的点录音说的是 fruit pies 这一招牌本身，不是 "食物种类丰富"——把口味多偷换成了出名理由。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（its delicious fruit pies ↔ Its tasty fruit pies delicious = tasty 同义替换）

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The whole village chips in to help, including the kids, who end up developing their baking skills at an early age.信号：范围词 whole 锁定参与主体 。答案信号是表范围的 whole 加动词短语 chips in to help：录音 The whole village chips in to help 直接点出帮忙的是 "整个村…

optionAnalysis.A: 答非所问：The contestants. 指参赛选手，录音里他们是 The exhausted and hungry racers are greeted with delightful pies（又累又饿、被村民用派招待）的一方，是被帮的人，不是来帮忙的人，方向正好弄反。 借用原文：It started with one person, Jan Newton

optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：People from the state of Idaho. 偷用了录音里真出现的地名 Idaho（Jan moved from Idaho 指 Jan 当年从 Idaho 搬来），但录音只说 Jan 一人来自 Idaho，从没说 "一群爱达荷人" 来帮忙办活动，纯属盗用地名拼凑出的人群。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（The whole village chips in to help ↔ The entire village whole village = entire village）

options.text: She owned a restaurant in Idaho.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Her rich and filling-fruit pies quickly got the racers' attention, and the village gained some fame as a result.信号：结果信号 as a result 点出她的贡献 。答案信号是结果状语 as a result：录音说她的派吸引选手注意，the village gained some fame as a result（村子因此出了名…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：She owned a restaurant in Idaho. 偷用了录音里真出现的地名 Idaho，但录音说 Jan 是 moved from Idaho（从 Idaho 搬出来）后才 opened a restaurant，餐馆其实是开在 Takotna，不是 Idaho——盗了地名却把餐馆地点安错了。 借用原文：Jan moved from Idaho with her husband in 1972

optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：She went to Alaska to compete in a race. 借了通篇反复出现的 race（比赛）一词，但录音说 Jan 是搬来开餐馆、做派招待选手，从没说她 "去阿拉斯加参赛"——去参赛的是 racers，不是 Jan，把比赛这条线张冠李戴到了她头上。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the village gained some fame as a result ↔ She helped the village to become famous 因她而村子出名 = 她帮村子出名）

paragraphs.text:
Nowadays you can't buy anything without being asked to provide a rating of a company's performance on a five-star scale.

I've been asked to rate my "store 26______ " on the EFTPOS terminal before I can pay. Even the most 27______ activities, such as calling Telstra or picking up a parcel from Australia Post, are followed by texts or emails with surveys asking, "How did we do?"

Online purchases are 28______ followed up by a customer satisfaction survey. Companies are so 29______ for a hit of stars that if you delete the survey the company sends you another one.

We're 30______ to rate our apps when we've barely had a chance to use them. One online course provider I use asks you what you think of the course after you've only completed 31______ 2 per cent of it.

Economist Jason Murphy says that companies use customer satisfaction ratings because a 32______ display of star feedback has become the nuclear power source of the modern economy.

However, you can't help but 33______ if these companies are basing their business on fabrications(捏造的东西). I 34______ that with online surveys I just click the 35______ that's closest to my mouse cursor(光标) to get the damn thing off my screen. Often the star rating I give has far more to do with the kind of day I'm having than the purchase I just made.

【答案】E（官方答案）
应填 E) experience
【原文】rate my "store __(26)__"，被要求打分的对象正是「store experience（购物体验）」——这是英语里固定说法。结合全文都在讲「给体验/服务打星」，experience 完全契合。
M) variety 义不搭，不评「种类」：variety 是「种类、多样性」，「store variety」指商品种类，但作者通篇评的是服务/体验的星级，不是评商品多不多；与 rate 的对象不符。
N) voyage 义不搭，航行无关：voyage 是「航行、海上旅程」，与在 EFTPOS 刷卡机上为购物打分的场景毫无关系，明显是干扰词。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: How do early career setbacks affect our long-term success? Failures can help us learn and overcome our fears. But disasters can still wound us. They can screw us up and set us back. Wouldn't it be nice if there was genuine, scientifically documented truth to the expression "what doesn't kill you makes you stronger"?

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: One way social scientists have probed the effects of career setbacks is to look at scientists of very similar qualifications. These scientists, for reasons that are mostly arbitrary, either just missed getting a research grant or just barely made it. In social sciences, this is known as examining "near misses" and "narrow wins" in areas where merit is subjective. That allows researchers to measure only the effects of being chosen or not. Studies in this area have found conflicting results. In the competitive game of biomedical science, research has been done on scientists who narrowly lost or won grant money. It suggests that narrow winners become even bigger winners down the line. In other words, the rich get richer.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: A 2018 study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, for example, followed researchers in the Netherlands. Researchers concluded that those who just barely qualified for a grant were able to get twice as much money within the next eight years as those who just missed out. And the narrow winners were 50 percent more likely to be given a professorship.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Others in the US have found similar effects with National Institutes of Health early-career fellowships launching narrow winners far ahead of close losers. The phenomenon is often referred to as the Matthew effect, inspired by the Bible's wisdom that to those who have, more will be given. There's a good explanation for the phenomenon in the book The Formula: The Universal Laws of Success by Albert Laszlo Barabasi. According to Barabasi, it's easier and less risky for those in positions of power to choose to hand awards and funding to those who've already been so recognized.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: This is bad news for the losers. Small early career setbacks seem to have a disproportionate effect down the line. What didn't kill them made them weaker. But other studies using the same technique have shown there's sometimes no penalty to a near miss. Students who just miss getting into top high schools or universities do just as well later in life as those who just manage to get accepted. In this case, what didn't kill them simply didn't matter. So is there any evidence that setbacks might actually improve our career prospects? There is now.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: In a study published in Nature Communications, Northwestern University sociologist Dashun Wang tracked more than 1,100 scientists who were on the border between getting a grant and missing out between 1990 and 2005. He followed various measures of performance over the next decade. These included how many papers they authored and how influential those papers were, as measured by the number of subsequent citations. As expected, there was a much higher rate of attrition(减员) among scientists who didn't get grants. But among those who stayed on, the close losers performed even better than the narrow winners. To make sure this wasn't by chance, Wang conducted additional tests using different performance measures. He examined how many times people were first authors on influential studies, and the like.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: One straightforward reason close losers might outperform narrow winners is that the two groups have comparable ability. In Wang's study, he selected the most determined, passionate scientists from the loser group and culled(剔除) what he deemed the weakest members of the winner group. Yet the persevering losers still came out on top. He thinks that being a close loser might give people a psychological boost, or the proverbial kick in the pants.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Utrecht University sociologist Arnout van de Rijt was the lead author on the 2018 paper showing the rich get richer. He said the new finding is apparently reasonable and worth some attention. His own work showed that although the narrow winners did get much more money in the near future, the actual performance of the close losers was just as good.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: He said the people who should be paying regard to the Wang paper are the funding agents who distribute government grant money. After all, by continuing to pile riches on the narrow winners, the taxpayers are not getting the maximum bang for their buck if the close losers are performing just as well or even better. There's a huge amount of time and effort that goes into the process of selecting who gets grants, he said, and the latest research shows that the scientific establishment is not very good at distributing money. "Maybe we should spend less money trying to figure out who is better than who," he said, suggesting that some more equal dividing up of money might be more productive and more efficient. Van de Rijt said he's not convinced that losing out gives people a psychological boost. It may yet be a selection effect. Even though Wang tried to account for this by culling the weakest winners, it's impossible to know which of the winners would have quit had they found themselves on the losing side.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: For his part, Wang said that in his own experience, losing did light a motivating fire. He recalled a recent paper he submitted to a journal, which accepted it only to request extensive editing, and then reversed course and rejected it. He submitted the unedited version to a more respected journal and got accepted.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: In sports and many areas of life, we think of failures as evidence of something we could have done better. We regard these disappointments as a fate we could have avoided with more careful preparation, different training, a better strategy, or more focus. And there it makes sense that failures show us the road to success. These papers deal with a kind of failure people have little control over—rejection. Others determine who wins and who loses. But at the very least, the research is starting to show that early setbacks don't have to be fatal. They might even make us better at our jobs. Getting paid like a winner, though? That's a different matter.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Boredom has become trendy. Studies point to how boredom is good for creativity and innovation, as well as mental health. It is found that people are more creative following the completion of a tedious task. When people are bored, they have an increase in "associative thought"—the process of making new connections between ideas, which is linked to innovative thinking. These studies are impressive, but in reality, the benefits of boredom may be related to having time to clear your mind, be quiet, or daydream.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: In our stimulation-rich world, it seems unrealistic that boredom could occur at all. Yet, there are valid reasons boredom may feel so painful. As it turns out, boredom might signal the fact that you have a need that isn't being met.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Our always-on world of social media may result in more connections, but they are superficial and can get in the way of building a real sense of belonging. Feeling bored may signal the desire for a greater sense of community and the feeling that you fit in with others around you. So take the step of joining an organization to build face-to-face relationships. You'll find depth that you won't get from your screen no matter how many likes you get on your post.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Similar to the need for belonging, bored people often report that they feel a limited sense of meaning. It's a fundamental human need to have a larger purpose and to feel like we're part of something bigger than ourselves. When people are bored, they're more likely to feel less meaning in their lives. If you want to reduce boredom and increase your sense of meaning, seek work where you can make a unique contribution, or find a cause you can support with your time and talent.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: If your definition of boredom is being quiet, mindful, and reflective, keep it up. But if you're struggling with real boredom and the emptiness it provokes, consider whether you might seek new connections and more significant challenges. These are the things that will genuinely relieve boredom and make you more effective in the process.

paragraphs.text: Can you remember what you ate yesterday? If asked, most people will be able to give a vague description of their main meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner. paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Why is this happening? We can point to at least three potential causes. One is the rise in obesity levels itself. Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Another cause is that the proportion of people who are trying to lose weight has been increasing over time. People who want to lose weight are more likely to under-report their eating—regardless of whether they are overweight or not. This may be driven partly by self-deception or "wishful thinking".

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The final potential cause is an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades—both in terms of how often they happen and how much they contribute to our overall energy intake. Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys.

paragraphs.label: G

Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines. If this works, it won't matter if they can't remember what they ate yesterday.

龙井(Longjing)是一种绿茶，主要产自中国东部沿海的浙江省。龙井茶独特的香味和口感为其赢得了"中国名茶"的称号，在中国深受大众的欢迎,在海外饮用的人也越来越多。龙井茶通常手工制作，其价格可能极其昂贵,也可能比较便宜，这取决于茶的生长地、采摘时间和制作工艺。龙井茶富含维生素C和其他多种有益健康的元素。经常喝龙井茶有助于减轻疲劳、延缓衰老。

【参考译文】
Longjing is a kind of green tea produced mainly in Zhejiang Province on the eastern coast of China. Its unique aroma and taste have earned Longjing the title of "China Famous Tea", and it is very popular among the public in China, with an increasing number of people drinking it abroad as well. Longjing tea is usually made by hand, and its price can be extremely high or relatively low, depending on where it grows, when it is picked, and how it is made. In addition, Longjing tea is rich in vitamin C and various other elements beneficial to health. Drinking it regularly helps relieve fatigue and delay aging.
